News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / Philippine Elections Philippine Elections Comelec expecting 80% voter turnout in Batanes special polls By: Chelsy Claire Perez - @inquirerdotnet Philippine Daily Inquirer / 04:16 PM November 26, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines—Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairperson George Erwin Garcia is expecting at least an 80 percent voter turnout in Batanes’ Nov. 28 special elections, citing the number of candidates and the expected participation of their supporters.
Batanes has around 13,000 registered voters, with four candidates vying for the province’s lone congressional district seat, Garcia said on Thursday.
“We have a total of 13,000 voters here and four candidates,” he said.
“Most likely, the candidates’ supporters, including their families, will go to the polling precincts separately.”
READ: Comelec starts printing ballots for Batanes special polls, Naga plebiscite
Garcia also observed that Batanes residents were already starting to return to the province to cast their votes.
While Garcia is hoping for at least 80 percent turnout, he stressed that encouraging people to exercise their right to vote remains more important than the actual turnout figure.
The Comelec will conduct the special elections through manual voting and counting, while pilot-testing the transmission of election results via text message to help speed up the canvassing process.
Garcia said the measure would address possible delays in transporting election results across the province’s six municipalities, particularly given its geographical conditions and challenging sea conditions in the afternoon.
READ: Comelec: Batanes polls’ canvassing results to be sent via messaging app
He assured that the initiative had been discussed with candidates, political parties, and other stakeholders. Official physical copies of the election documents would also be delivered for verification.
Batanes will hold the Nov. 28 special elections to choose a new representative for its lone congressional district following the death of Rep. Ciriaco Gato Jr. last September.
